thread.title: How Microsoft Beat Apple (Capital Market Laboratories) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Brian Bain
title: How Microsoft Beat Apple (Capital Market Laboratories) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
The story behind the interview: Ophir Gottlieb writes as "Capital Market Laboratories" and is a leading authority on Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and other leading tech companies.
I tracked down Ophir after a recent article of his discussing notable shifts taking place in Apple's revenue streams.
For those who prefer to read, my full interview notes are copied below.
Link to Capital Market Laboratories original article: Apple Stunned Everyone - Did Something It Has Never Done Before
Interview Notes: While beating EPS they missed on revenue and missed on iPhone units
Normally would be a disaster
Stock rose anyway
Transformation of company of something larger than just a phone company
Apple services (iTunes, iCloud, etc.)
270M paid subs
Very different kind of revenue
Recurring revenue unlike hardware
Companies re getting valued by recurring revenue
$9.2B in last quarter
Up 30% y over y
Should double by 2020
P/E and P/S can improve dramatically
Ex: Microsoft 360 and Cloud
CEO shift in MSFT was huge due to strategic shift
MSFT earnings were collapsing between 2014-16 but stock was up 80% because of shift to recurring revenue model
Wall Street likes transparency and predictability
How do we know how many iPhones will sell next quarter? We don't
Wall Street like predictability
Facebook ( FB ) and Google ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) have higher multiples because of recurring revenue
This has been a really remarkable accomplishment by Tim Cook
Keeping earnings growing while shifting strategy is significant
People misunderstood how success happens for Apple with hardware
Ex: first few iPhones were a flop
First Apple Watch outsold first iPhone
Apple creates cognition
People didn't know they wanted music in their pockets
People didn't know they wanted a computer on their wrist
Apple Watch growing 56% year over year in shipping volume
All other watch competitors are shrinking
Apple Watch pushes Apple Services
When Apple makes hardware, people listen
Tim Cook has said over and over that Watch is growing
Apple Watch could take on scale at Apple
Ex: 15+% of revenue
Apple A/R
Apple will do it and it will be gigantic
Apple Social Network
Ex: iMessage emoticons, etc.
Patents for social network
Meeting in person over A/R
Apple doesn't care what you need
Apple sells to what people want
They do it better than any other company
They tell you that you want it and then sell it to you
How does Apple reach $2T?
There are still markets large enough
Public cloud
Speakers
Cars
Advertising
Bullish thesis for Apple
Services is growing gangbusters
High margin
Recurring revenue
Attached to every device
Won't give you NVIDIA returns but will be a great investment
Growing revenue
Next Steps... I hope you enjoyed this interview.
